1. Purpose. To maximize Navy Reserve Force warfighting readiness through aligned planning efforts
and prioritized resource execution, this policy augments governing directives (references (a) through (r)).
2. Scope and Applicability. This notice applies to Commander, Navy Reserve Force
(COMNAVRESFOR), its subordinate commands, and all Reserve Program Directors (RPD). Associated
members must be familiar with and comply with the contents of governing directives in their entirety.
3. Goals. Under reference (a), in keeping with Acting Secretary of the Navy (SECNAV), Chief of Naval
Operations (CNO), and Acting Chief of Navy Reserve (CNR) direction to our Navy and Navy Reserve:
a. To maintain 80% mission and mobilization readiness (warfighting readiness) throughout the fiscal
year (FY), delivering a ready, trained, combat-credible force that is seamlessly integrated (no daylight
between the active component and reserve component) anytime, anywhere, to fight and win.
b. To prioritize Reserve Personnel Navy (RPN) execution toward strategic depth and warfighting
readiness while delivering necessary operational support to the Fleet and Joint Force.

16 Sep 2026
2
4. Planning Policy. Warfighting readiness is our North Star and reference (b) is our chart. Note that:
a. Annual Training (AT) entitlements must be used by the Force on warfighting readiness objectives.
b. Inactive Duty Training (IDT) period entitlem ents must be prioritized by Unit Mobilization Unit
Identification Codes (UMUIC) to achieve warfighting and unit readiness objectives.
c. Discretionary RPN funds should be prioritized by the Force toward achievement of warfighting
readiness objectives over ad hoc operational support (note paragraph 8, Active Duty for Training (ADT)).
5. Mobilization Readiness Policy. Mobilization readiness encompasses completion of necessary medical,
administrative, and training requirements to be deployable. The two categories of mobilization driving
readiness requirements are Mobilization-to-Billet (M2B) and Individual Augmentation (IA).
a. Compliance. In line with the responsibil ities outlined in reference (c), UMUIC Commanding
Officers (CO) and Officers-in-Charge (OIC) will ensure completion and annual verification of all
mobilization deployment screening items, commonly referred to as billet-based suitability screening
(BBSS). For M2B, mobilization deployment screening items are defined in reference (d) 3060-080 which
includes the minimum requirements to activate Reserve Sailors for IA as defined in reference (d)
3060-070. UMUIC COs/OICs and RPDs must notify Navy Reserve Activities (NRA) within 30 days of
any known readiness deficiencies for assigned members and assist NRAs with addressing mobilization
readiness requirements. Screening requirements for M2B versus IA differ as follows:
(1) M2B: As with Active Duty for Operational Support (ADOS), Sailors must screen and meet
minimum requirements to activate before mobilization orders are generated (see reference (d) 3060-070).
(2) IA: Sailors are screened for their mobilization assignment after receiving orders.
b. Deployment Readiness Training (DRT). Select ed Reserve (SELRES) Sailors must participate in
DRT once every five years to receive training, education, and information that enhances mobilization
readiness. Echelon 4 and 5 commands are responsible for updating a member's Fleet Training
Management and Planning System (FLTMPS) record to document this training.
c. AT for SELRES Sailors Identified for Mobili zation. Once a SELRES Sailor is identified for
mobilization with an Individual Mobilization Status (IMS) code of R## or RC1, mobilization screening
requirements supersede other required training. NRA COs and RPDs must coordinate to prioritize use of
AT for completion of mobilization screening. Any AT remaining may be used for other training
requirements, and other order types (e.g. ADT) may also be used for training requirements.
6. Satisfactory Participation Policy. Unit COs/OICs must counsel assigned SELRES Sailors on
satisfactory participation requirements per subparagraphs 6a and 6b, below. Failure to meet minimum
participation requirements may result in adverse administrative action per references (d) through (g).
a. Active Duty (AD) Requirement. Per references (e) enclosure 7, (f) Chapter 13, (d) 1001-150, and
(g) 1571-010, SELRES Sailors must perform at least 12 days of AD each FY (14 days for operational
units) (SELRES Sailors who affiliate on 1 June or later are exempt from this requirement). SELRES
Sailors may meet the FY AD requirement through any combination of AT, ADT, or other duty types
COMNAVRESFORNOTE 1001
16 Sep 2026
3
listed in reference (g) 1571-010 paragraph 4 (“Substitution”). This substitution does not require higher
review. See paragraph 7 for more guidance on AT and paragraph 8 for more guidance on ADT.
(1) Documentation of AD Requirement. NRAs are reminded that only AT or ADT orders can
automatically reflect completion of the participation requirement, which occurs once 12 or more days are
recorded by electronic muster (e-Muster) in NSIPS. For other AD types (non-e-Muster, ADOS,
mobilization, recall, et cetera), the NRA must manually make an NSIPS entry of “C” to mark the
requirement as complete per reference (g) 1571-010 paragraph 5.
(2) AT Waiver Requests. Per reference (g) 1571-010 paragraph 6, members who cannot meet
their AD requirement must submit a NAVRES 1571/15 Annual Training Waiver Request to explain the
circumstances that prevent completion. An approved AT waiver satisfies the annual AD participation
requirement. AT waiver approval authority typically rests with the NRA CO. The NRA will make an
NSIPS entry of “W” to reflect an approved AT waiver per reference (g) 1571-010 paragraph 5. When
evaluating AT waiver requests, approvers will factor exceptions in reference (g) 1571-010 paragraph 6:
(a) Cancellation. Training opportunity canceled or modified by the supported command that
precludes attainment of minimum required days of AD.
(b) Administrative. Not medically qualified or prohibited from performing AD.
(c) Hardship. Undue personal hardship exists that precludes AD.
b. Inactive Duty Requirement. Per references (e) enclosure (7), (f) Chapter 12, (d) 1001-150, and
(g) 1001-010, SELRES Sailors are required to accomplish favorable adjudication of at least 40 (of 48)
regular IDT periods per FY. The definition of a favorable adjudication is a “Present” or “Authorized
Absence.” Unit COs/OICs must consider an individual’s entitled IDT period completion rate prior to
approving additional IDT periods. See paragraph 9 for more guidance on IDT.
7. Annual Training (AT) Policy. See reference (g) 1571-010. AT orders are involuntary orders
scheduled in coordination between the UMUIC CO/OIC and supported command RPD, as required per
reference (f). Unit leadership and RPDs should consider the possibility of budget shortfalls and inform
Sailors that AT may become unavailable later in the FY if the member has completed other qualifying
AD training. See paragraph 10 for additional order and travel guidance.
a. Application. AT is the primary means to satisfy paragraph 6a participation requirements and
should be used to advance mission readiness whenever possible. Execution of AT prior to of other types
of AD (i.e. ADT, ADOS) is preferred; however, to allow commands the flexibility to match mission
priorities with funding requirements, an “AT first” policy is not mandatory but deviations should be
defensible. See paragraph 5c regarding AT for SELRES Sailors identified for Mobilization.
b. AT Deadlines
(1) 1 May. SELRES Sailors with known personal hardships must submit AT waiver requests to
their chain of command (COC) per reference (g) 1571-010. Emergent AT waivers may be submitted for
consideration through the end of the FY (see paragraph 6a(2) for more information on AT waivers).
COMNAVRESFORNOTE 1001
16 Sep 2026
4
(2) 30 June. NRAs must have all properly submitted or routed AT orders “saved and routed” in
the Navy Reserve Orders Writing System (NROWS) for the remainder of the FY. Fund approval will
only be guaranteed for AT orders forwarded by the NRA Orders Specialist (OS) by this deadline. NRAs
must continue to save and route orders for approval after this date, but available funds across the Force
may require movement of AT resources to other accounts.
(3) 30 September. NRAs must ensure all AT waiver requests are adjudicated and appropriate
code entries made in NSIPS per paragraph 6a(2) and reference (g) 1571-010.
c. Directed AT. Each year there are Sailors who fail to complete paragraph 6a participation
requirements. To assist them in meeting their obligation to achieve satisfactory participation, the
following policy is in effect:
(1) 31 May. COMNAVRESFOR N31 w ill promulgate the list of members who have neither
achieved satisfactory AD participation nor have associated NROWS orders committed.
(2) No Later Than 14 June. Echelon 4 commands and NRAs will contact each unit CO/OIC
under their cognizance who have one or more Sailors out of compliance with paragraph 6a participation
requirements and remind them of annual AD participation requirements. UMUIC leadership is ultimately
responsible for member execution to advance warfighting readiness and is responsible for the selection of
dates and locations of Directed AT as well as generation of associated NROWS requirements. Training
Readiness Unit Identification Code (TRUIC) COCs will be included in these communications for
awareness and assistance. NRA involvement is required due to their access to AT fund approval.
(3) No Later Than 30 June. Directed AT orders may be issued to all Sailors who have not
satisfied their AD participation requirement. The order length must be of duration required for the
member to achieve a satisfactory year per paragraph 6a and must be completed by the end of the FY per
paragraph 7b(3). For SELRES Sailors in mobilization billets, the supported command RPD will write the
NROWS requirement in coordination with UMUIC leadership, and the UMUIC will then write Directed
AT orders using NROWS unit approver and reviewer profiles. For SELRES Sailors who are In
Assignment Processing (IAP), the NRA CO has the authority to issue Directed AT orders with the goal of
assigning in-rate training where available with other UMUICs hosted by the NRA. When such
opportunities do not exist, the member will be directed to complete their AT at the NRA to build
mobilization readiness. Local AT NROWS requirements will be written by the NRA or echelon 4. Any
Directed AT orders written must comply with Split AT travel restrictions (paragraph 7e).
(4) No Later Than 30 September. If, due to unique individual challenges, the Sailor is unable to
execute Directed AT orders, then an AT waiver may be submitted per paragraph 6a(2). NRAs must
ensure approved waivers are recorded in NSIPS by the end of the FY per paragraph 7b(3).
d. Exceptional AT (E-AT). AT beyond 14 days is known and referred to as ‘Exceptional AT.’
(1) Limit. An individual Sailor will not execute more than 29 days of AT in an FY. This limit is
routinely reduced over the course of an FY, which is announced by RPD Mailbag (“CNRFC N31 RPD”
subscription on ForceConnect) and updated on the COMNAVRESFOR N31 SharePoint. All travel days
are included when calculating a Sailor’s total number of AT days for the FY.
COMNAVRESFORNOTE 1001
16 Sep 2026
5
(2) Controlled E-AT. Controlled E-AT guidance is per COMNAVRESFOR N31 Standard
Operating Procedure (SOP) 23, available under ‘N31 Files’ on the N31 SharePoint at:
https://FlankSpeed.SharePoint-mil.US/sites/CNRFC_N31/SitePages/Home.aspx. Controlled E-AT is E-
AT available on a limited basis for specific communities’ and units’ use after COMNAVRESFOR
reductions to Force-wide E-AT limitations are imposed. Events identified for Controlled E-AT will be
able to retain E-AT after other AT reductions are directed for the rest of the Force, but only as long as AT
funds permit. Controlled E-AT designation is not a guarantee that 29 days of AT will be available for the
entire FY. The best way to secure more than 14 days of AT support is to route orders as early as possible.
(a) Designation. Supported command proposals for Controlled E-AT should be discussed
with and nominations will be routed via the pillar lead (or designated representative). Only the pillar lead
(or designated representative) will discuss proposals with and submit nominations to COMNAVRESFOR
N31 directly. N31 will consolidate nominations for the COMNAVRESFOR Executive Committee
(EXCOM), which will then present nominations to the COMNAVRESFOR Deputy for approval.
Approved Controlled E-AT events will be promulgated per COMNAVRESFOR N31 SOP 23.
(b) Travel Limitations. Split AT policy (paragraph 7e, below) also applies to Controlled AT.
e. Split AT. Split AT guidance is per COMNAVRESFOR N31 SOP 23.
(1) Without Travel. Authorized with no minimum day requirement restrictions. No request for
an exception to policy (ETP) is required.
(2) With Travel. Authorized, but limited to four funded travel legs (typically two sets of orders
with one round trip each). Split AT travel may be utilized on a single order set with ‘For Further
Assignment’ (i.e. travel to multiple per diem locations on one order) or when executing back-to-back
orders of a different type in order to mitigate AT travel expenses and promote AT fund availability for the
Force in the remaining FY. This limit on travel legs applies to the entire Force, including those
communities and exercises approved for Controlled E-AT. In the event AT funding requires the
termination of Split AT during the FY, any member having executed two or more travel legs that year
may be prohibited from any further travel costs against the AT account in that FY. For additional travel
via the supported command, see paragraph 10f.
(a) Duration. Split AT orders with travel (each order set) must be no less than five days
inclusive of travel days. Orders for less than five days with travel should use IDT Travel (IDTT)
(paragraph 9c) in conjunction with IDT periods or additional IDT periods. ADT orders of less than five
days are permitted within the availability of the supported command RPD.
(b) Calculation and E-AT. Travel days are included when calculating the total number of AD
days in an FY and are considered training days for the purposes of satisfactory participation. When
planning Split AT with travel, particularly when E-AT funding is a factor, it is important to understand
how a reduction in the E-AT limit affects orders. When the E-AT day limit is reduced to 14 days for the
fiscal year, any remaining AT days with travel must be calculated against this new limit. For instance, if
the member has already completed a nine-day set of AT orders and E-AT is reduced to 14 days, then the
member will only be authorized a maximum of five days for their second set of Split AT orders.
Furthermore, per paragraph 7e(2)(a) above, in this scenario, the second order must be exactly five days to
meet both the minimum order length for Split AT and the maximum annual E-AT days remaining. If a
member requires AT in excess of the current E-AT limit in order to complete paragraph 6a participation
COMNAVRESFORNOTE 1001
16 Sep 2026
6
requirements (e.g. previously completed 10 days of AT but E-AT is reduced to 14 days), then the member
should complete AT without travel, substitute other qualifying AD (reference (g) 1571-010 paragraph 4),
submit a waiver (paragraph 6a(2)), or submit an ETP request (paragraph 7e(4)).
(3) Appropriateness. AT must NOT be used when IDT is the appropriate funding type (e.g. drill
weekend (DWE) at TRUIC, UMUIC, or alternate drill site).
(4) Exceptions. Requests for exceptions (e.g. travel for less than five days, more than four travel
legs) may be considered via ETP request. Refer to COMNAVRESFOR N31 SOP 23 for guidance.
(5) Guidance Updates. Throughout the FY, COMNAVRESFOR N31 will monitor and publish
direction via RPD Mailbag informing the Force of fund availability with respect to Split AT with travel.
8. Active Duty for Training (ADT) Policy. Per reference (g) 1571-010, ADT is a period of AD intended
to support a specific training requirement. ADT-Special funding is distributed per recommendations of
the COMNAVRESFOR EXCOM. ADT-Schools funding is centrally managed by COMNAVRESFOR
N7 (see paragraph 8c, below). See paragraph 10 for additional order and travel guidance.
a. Application. RPDs are strongly encouraged to allocate ADT-Special per individual training
plans (ITP) aligned to warfighting readiness. Per reference (e), the primary purpose of ADT is to
provide individual or unit readiness training. Support to mission requirements may occur incidental to
performing ADT, but long-term orders that do not principally provide warfighting readiness value are
antithetical to this guidance and to the philosophies laid out by reference (a). As such,
COMNAVRESFOR N31 will review all ADT orders that exceed 179 days of support to the same
command within a fiscal year, regardless of any break in service, via the NROWS headquarters (HQ)
waiver ‘ADT Days.’ To meet COMNAVRESFOR N31 validation, RPDs will provide pillar leads with
reasoning for keeping a Sailor on extended training orders and COMNAVRESFOR N31 will not clear
this HQ waiver without corresponding pillar RPD approval.
b. Voluntary Training Unit (VTU) Use of ADT. Performance of ADT by VTU members is limited
to 29 days per year, per references (f) section 312 and (d) 1001-150 Note 3.
c. ADT-Schools Requirements. Consistent with reference (a), COMNAVRESFOR N7 will prioritize
available ADT-Schools funds and training time to build high-end warfighting readiness.
(1) Requirement Vetting. COMNAVRESFOR N7 will verify ADT-Schools requests in NROWS
to make fiscally disciplined investments in programmed mobilization billet training for individual Sailors
as aligned with a documented requirement per the following subparagraphs. COMNAVRESFOR N7 will
consider training requirements valid only if documented in FLTMPS, Total Force Manpower
Management System (TFMMS), or T-Ready. Requirements not found in these systems are considered
invalid.
(a) Navy Enlisted Classification (NEC)/Addi tional Qualification Designation (AQD) Award.
COMNAVRESFOR N7 will fund orders for SELRES Sailors to complete schools awarding NECs/AQDs
on their assigned mobilization billet as defined in TFMMS. COMNAVRESFOR N7 will use the Navy
Reserve Readiness Module (NRRM) Individual Readiness Jacket and/or NSIPS data as reflected in the
COMNAVRESFORCOM N1 SELRES Manning Cube as its derivative data sources to determine billet-
required NECs/AQDs and current individual NECs/AQDs for each SELRES Sailor.
COMNAVRESFORNOTE 1001
16 Sep 2026
7
(b) Professional Development. COMNAVRESFOR N7 will fund orders for SELRES Sailors
with confirmed quotas to professional development courses specified in paragraph 11a.
(c) Unit-Level Training. COMNAVRESFOR N7 will fund orders for SELRES Sailors to
attend schools to complete unit-level training requirements as documented on the command training plan
report in FLTMPS.
(d) Exceptions. Requests for an exception to fund ADT-Schools orders for undocumented
billet or unit-level requirements must indicate that the RPD, supported command, Type Commander
(TYCOM), or Fleet is engaged in the process of documenting the new requirement in TFMMS or
FLTMPS and will be evaluated on a case-by-case basis if adequate justification is provided within the
NROWS requirement. See paragraph 8c(4) for additional guidance.
(2) Quota Management. To ensure proper quota management, NROWS orders must be
submitted, saved, and routed by the NRA OS no later than 30 days prior to the start date of the orders. It
is the responsibility of the Sailor and the Sailor’s COC to cancel unused quotas as soon as possible, but no
later than 14 days prior to the start of the course, to allow other potential students the opportunity to train.
(3) Routing Deadline. No later than 30 June, Sailors and NRAs must save and route ADT-
Schools orders in NROWS to allow for end of year funding prioritization. To comply with this deadline,
NROWS ADT-Schools orders requested during the FY fourth quarter (where the student does not have a
confirmed seat) can be routed with the following justification block verbiage, “Member is registered for
the course and awaiting quota confirmation.”
(4) Additional Guidance. The COMNAVR ESFOR ADT-Schools (N71) SharePoint page
contains comprehensive ADT-Schools orders vetting criteria and additional ADT-Schools guidance and
can be located at: https://SharePoint.NavyReserve.Navy.mil/CNRFC/N-Codes/N7/ADTSchools/.
Current ADT-Schools guidance (COMNAVRESFOR N7 SOP 07) can be found on the Warfighting
Readiness Guidance SharePoint at: https://SharePoint.NavyReserve.Navy.mil/CNRFC/N-
Codes/N7/Pages/ForceGenerationGuidance.aspx.
9. Inactive Duty Training (IDT) Policy. See reference (g) 1570-010. Member-entitled IDT periods are
the primary means of completing paragraph 6b participation requirements. Travel in conjunction with
IDT periods is possible with IDTT (paragraph 9c) and IDT Reimbursable (IDT-R) (paragraph 9d).
a. Fourth Quarter Scheduling. Unit and NRA COs are entrusted to understand and execute
COMNAVRESFOR’s intent to support legitimate FY fourth quarter unit or supported command
requirements while minimizing financial risks. To reduce financial risk from unexecuted IDT periods,
NRAs will not allow members to “hold” or “park” IDT periods in quarter four. NRAs must not approve
reschedule requests for members that would result in having more than 16 IDT periods scheduled in
quarter four nor allow members to schedule more than six regular IDT periods in September. As soon as
possible, unit COs must provide justification to the NRA explaining circumstances that warrant deviating
from this policy. Such justification must detail both how the rescheduled IDT periods support a valid
mission or training requirement and reason for confidence the drills will be completed. If Sailors desire
additional duty beyond the 12 IDT periods originally allotted for quarter four but the reschedule request
does not meet the requirements of this paragraph, then Sailors will coordinate with their unit leadership
and RPD for additional authorized voluntary IDT (non-pay), Additional Training Periods (ATP),
Additional Flying and Flight Training Periods (AFTP), and Readiness Management Periods (RMP).
COMNAVRESFORNOTE 1001
16 Sep 2026
8
b. Additional IDT Periods. Per reference (e), ‘additional IDT periods’ are ATPs, AFTPs, and RMPs.
(1) RPD Guidance. RPDs are responsible for advising unit leadership on availability,
distribution, purpose, and execution of additional IDT periods for assigned units per reference (g)
1570-010. In Operational Support Plan Additional Drill Execution Spreadsheet (OSPADES), RPDs must
closely monitor additional IDT period allocations against actual funds execution.
(2) Unit Guidance. Per reference (g) 1570-010, TRUIC COs/OICs are responsible for approving
additional IDT periods in the Electronic Drill Management (EDM) system and managing available
allocated additional IDT periods. Unit approval of additional IDT periods in EDM serves as verification
to the NRA that the unit has confirmed funding is available in OSPADES (so an additional letter from the
unit to the NRA for approval of individual additional IDT periods is not required).
c. Inactive Duty Training Travel (IDTT). As detailed in reference (h), IDTT funding provides travel
and per diem for Sailors performing IDT periods away from their primary drill site. Supported
commands, Navy Reserve Region Readiness and Mobilization Commands (REDCOM), and unit
leadership must prioritize available IDTT funding toward necessary training that builds unit readiness and
contributes to warfighting readiness. See paragraph 10 for additional order and travel guidance.
(1) Application. IDTT funding should be used to bring non-locally assigned Sailors to their
UMUIC or to the supported command. Per reference (h), IDTT cannot be used for travel at the
permanent IDT site. Individual training on such travel should be used to maximize warfighting readiness
and M2B training at the UMUIC location, Fleet concentration areas, or the supported command.
Additionally, IDTT may be used for group training, which ensures SELRES teams are trained, ready to
activate, and can fight at their supported command on day one. RPDs must plan, prioritize, and fund all
non-locally assigned Sailor travel to the maximum extent achievable to meet specific supported command
additional training and mobilization requirements. This procedural approach eliminates confusion about
the funding source for IDTT. Navy Reserve echelon 4 commands will fund IDTT for Sailors
administratively assigned to echelon 5 activities within the cognizant echelon 4 area of responsibility for
baseline mobilization readiness (medical, dental, legal, et cetera) and Sailors assigned to readiness support
units (RSU) in an IAP status.
(2) Drill Coordination. Prior to approval of IDTT, members must be approved in EDM for
associated IDT periods or additional IDT periods covering each day of the reporting period (i.e. no drills
required on the travel day). After IDTT execution, if IDT periods or additional IDT periods were not
scheduled then IDT pay will not be retroactively authorized, resulting only in approval of non-pay
additional IDT periods.
d. Inactive Duty Training Reimbursable (IDT-R). Per reference (i) 032304, IDT-R funding provides
reimbursement for travel for selected members of the Navy Reserve to address critical skill shortfalls in
support of increased unit readiness. Sailors who meet eligibility requirements and travel 150 miles or
greater from their primary residence to their drill site may apply per reference (j) (or successive guidance)
via the COMNAVRESFOR N12 SharePoint. Eligible members who opt-in to the IDT-R program will be
reimbursed up to the limit prescribed in reference (i) 032304. Members are limited to 12 reimbursable
round trips, and this program may be restricted due to budgetary constraints.
COMNAVRESFORNOTE 1001
16 Sep 2026
9
10. Order and Travel Policy. See reference (h). Liquidation of NROWS orders and Defense Travel
System (DTS) vouchers is a Force priority and must be incorporated into routine NRA and unit business.
a. Travel Time. Travel time is considered the time required to arrive on station to begin the mission.
Time required to return to the ending location is part of the mission and included in the end of the order
period, per reference (i), and both must be considered when calculating approved order length,
particularly for compliance with AT limits described in paragraph 7.
b. NROWS Routing. Orders should be submitted well in advance to meet Continental U.S.
(CONUS) or Outside Continental U.S. (OCONUS) approval goals. Longer lead-times facilitate travel
coordination and avoid short lead-time travel challenges. To ensure timely commitment and approval of
orders, NRA OSs must save and route all valid orders within five business days of receipt. For emergent
missions or requirements, Sailors and unit leadership should promptly contact their NRA for assistance.
(1) AT. The default goal is to fund approve AT orders 45 days prior to start. NRAs will
continuously fund and approve all valid AT orders beginning within 45 days, as funding from REDCOM
comptrollers allows. This funding window may be expanded later in the FY and will be communicated
via RPD Mailbag, if changed. Fund approvers will coordinate directly with COMNAVRESFOR N31 to
approve orders outside of the prescribed AT funding window (only for official passports, see paragraph
10g). See paragraphs 7b and 7c for additional AT deadline information.
(2) ADT. The goal is to fund approve ADT orders 90 days prior to start. Fund approvers will
coordinate directly with COMNAVRESFOR N31 to approve orders outside of the prescribed ADT
funding window (only for official passports, see paragraph 10g). Per reference (k) enclosure (5) and
reference (h) section 2, all ADT orders over 29 days must be screened by the NRA OS. See paragraphs
8a for additional ADT duration control and 8c(2) and 8c(3) for ADT-Schools deadlines.
(3) IDTT. The goal is to fund approve IDTT 90 days prior to start. Appropriate fund approvers
will continuously fund approve all valid IDTT that begins within 90 days, as practicable and as funding
allows.
c. Travel Authorizations. The goal is for travel to be approved (via DTS) no later than 14 days
before order start date for CONUS orders (30 days for OCONUS). Timely routing and approval of DTS
authorizations helps limit travel costs against AT/ADT/IDTT accounts, as less timely approval results in
higher airfare costs and Certificates of Non-Availability (CNA) which tend to increase per diem and
rental car costs. A member’s failure to expeditiously route their DTS authorization upon order approval
may be used as grounds for denial of additional travel orders. Travel reimbursement depends upon order
type; IDTT is calculated from the permanent IDT site, while AT and ADT orders are calculated from the
primary residence. For further information, refer to reference (h) or an NRA approving official.
d. Orders Endorsements. SELRES and VTU Sailors on orders must ensure reporting and detaching
endorsements are completed by the supported command prior to completion of duty. For AT and ADT,
NSIPS e-Muster is the primary means of endorsement but in extenuating circumstances (e.g. reporting
command does not have a Command Pay and Personnel Administrator (CPPA) assigned to field or afloat
duty, prolonged system issues, or any other circumstance that does not allow for e-Muster) handwritten
and stamped endorsements remain acceptable. For IDTT vouchers, handwritten remains the only means
of endorsement because member accountability is conducted via EDM.
COMNAVRESFORNOTE 1001
16 Sep 2026
10
(1) Planning for e-Muster. When generating an NROWS requirement, Requirement Owners
should consider the unit identification code (UIC) entered under ‘Reporting Information,’ as only a CPPA
associated with that UIC in NSIPS can conduct e-Muster for a reporting Reservist.
(2) e-Muster Retrieval. Electronic endorsements are available in a Sailor’s NSIPS ‘Member Self
Service’ profile by selecting ‘Employee Self Service’ under ‘Menu,’ then ‘View’ under ‘Electronic
Service Record,’ then ‘AT/ADT Orders Signature Page’, then verifying endorsements, and downloading
the applicable .pdf file. If electronic endorsements are expected but missing, then the member should
promptly contact a CPPA associated with the reporting UIC in their orders.
e. Travel Vouchers. Within five business days of orders completion, SELRES and VTU Sailors must
submit their travel voucher including a copy of their endorsed orders. Endorsements are required (see
paragraph 10d, above). For electronic endorsements, a complete set of blank orders must accompany the
endorsed AT or ADT signature page from the NSIPS ‘Member Self Service’ profile. Unsubmitted
travel vouchers are automatically zeroed out after 45 days in accordance with reference (l).
f. Supported Command Travel. If supported commands require SELRES or VTU members to travel
to multiple duty locations, then additional travel legs can be paid under an active duty DTS profile created
for the member by the supported command. If there are questions about this method, supported command
RPDs (not units or individual members) should contact COMNAVRESFOR N33.
g. Special Issuance Passport (i.e. “Official Passport” or “Maroon Passport”). The State Department
requires approved official orders to begin processing an official passport. For orders requiring an official
passport, NRAs and RPDs may fund approve as soon as screening is complete. The fund approver will
need to coordinate directly with COMNAVRESFOR N31 (via email) to approve orders outside of
paragraph 10b funding windows. The Foreign Clearance Guide (FCG) contains theater and country
information pertaining to entry requirements, to include when use of an official passport is required.
h. Unit Administration. Unit COs/OICs must inco rporate order and travel voucher liquidation as part
of routine unit administration. Should a member not execute orders, this includes action to immediately
cancel both the NROWS order application and the associated DTS authorization, when applicable.
i. NRA Administration. NRAs must monitor and work to reconcile orders and travel voucher
liquidation weekly. NRAs are authorized to suspend subsequent orders until all required documentation
has been submitted to satisfy the liquidation of any previous order. In the event of a disruption to routine
pay for AT/ADT, NRAs will contact the Reserve Center of Excellence (RCOE), Norfolk. Disruptions
include, but are not limited to, order modification of executed orders, use of wet signature rather than
e-Muster, or any other pay or personnel record change incurred during order execution that could disrupt
proper automated processing.
11. Personnel Policy
a. Professional Development
(1) Officer Leadership Training. Reserve Senior Leadership Course (RSLC) (two days) is
designed for the paygrades of O-5 (to include O-5 selects) and O-6. Reserve Intermediate Leadership
Course (RILC) (two days) is designed for the paygrades of O-3 and O-4 to promote professional growth
in ethics, self-awareness, leader development, and decision making for officers assigned to department

head positions. Officers are highly encouraged to attend at a five-year periodicity consistent with
reference (m). ADT-Schools is available to SELRES officers for all leadership training courses. The
mission number for officer leadership training can be found on the COMNAVRESFOR N7 ADT-Schools
SharePoint page at: https://SharePoint.NavyReserve.Navy.mil/CNRFC/N-Codes/N7/ADTSchools/.
(2) Navy Officer Development School (ODS). As update to reference (n), COMNAVRESFOR
N7 manages application of the direct commission officer manpower availability status (MAS) code
(“DCO”) for direct commission officers who have not completed ODS. The DCO MAS code initiates an
NROWS hard hold prohibiting execution of other ADT and AT orders prior to the completion of Navy
ODS. COMNAVRESFOR N7 is the only organization authorized to remove the DCO MAS code from a
Reserve officer's record. Per reference (n), a new direct commission officer’s first set of orders will be
issued to complete Navy ODS. By-passing the DCO MAS code prior to completion of ODS is at the
discretion of COMNAVRESFORCOM N7 on a case-by-case basis with a confirmed ODS quota. Direct
commission officers will attend the full five-week ODS course using ADT-Schools orders. Direct
commission officers must successfully complete the course within one year of commissioning. For
schedules, see the Catalog of Navy Training Courses (CANTRAC) at:
https://app.prod.CeTARS.Training.Navy.mil/CANTRAC/Vol2.html. Waivers to extend beyond one year
from commissioning date may be approved based on ODS class quota availability.
(3) Information Warfare (IW) Officer Accession Training. Commander, Naval Information Force
Reserve (COMNAVIFORES) N7 manages the “TIW” MAS code for officers who have not completed
IW accession training. Upon removal of the DCO MAS code, COMNAVIFORES N7 will assign the
TIW MAS code to IW officers who require follow-on training per COMNAVIFORES policy, which is
meant to ensure completion of required IW training within three years of commissioning. Upon
completion of training, the member will provide proof to unit leadership and COMNAVIFORES N7 to
remove the TIW MAS code.
(4) Enlisted Leadership Development (ELD). Per reference (o), ELD courses are advancement
eligibility requirements that must be completed in consecutive days of study. ELD completion is a
prerequisite for taking the Navy-wide Advancement Exam for E-6 and E-7. ELD is a prerequisite for
promotion eligibility to E-8. Sailors can search for ELD courses via CANTRAC:
https://app.prod.CeTARS.Training.Navy.mil/CANTRAC/Vol2.html. COMNAVRESFOR N7 will
provide ADT-Schools funding for SELRES Sailors that have confirmed quotas to attend ELD courses
that are built in eNTRS, subject to funding availability. ELD hosts and facilitators can request a course to
be built in eNTRS by coordinating with the appropriate Regional Coordinator and COMNAVRESFOR
ELD team at NavyRESFORELD@US.Navy.mil. Advancement eligibility attendance requirements:
(a) E-7 Sailors: Chief Petty Officer Leadership Development Course (CPOLDC) (five days)
(b) E-6 Sailors: Advanced Leadership Development Course (ALDC) (four days)
(c) E-5 Sailors: Intermediate Leadership Development Course (ILDC) (three days)
(d) E-3 and E-4 Sailors: Foundational Leadership Development Course (FLDC) (three days)
(While not an advancement eligibility requirement, E-3/E-4 Sailors are highly encouraged to attend.)

(5) Senior Enlisted Academy (SEA). Per references (d) 1306-925 and (o), Senior Chief Petty
Officers (SCPO) selected in FY 2017 and later must complete SEA to be eligible for advancement to
Master Chief Petty Officer (MCPO). All future SEA students must have completed Enlisted Joint
Professional Military Education II (EJPME II) prior to applying for a quota for enrollment. Subject to
availability, COMNAVRESFOR N7 will provide ADT-Schools funding for SELRES Sailors to attend.
There are typically two dedicated two-week SELRES-only SEA courses scheduled per FY. SCPOs and
Chief Petty Officers (CPO) who have completed CPOLDC and desire to attend SEA must plan to attend
one of these two SELRES SEA courses. SELRES quotas for the three-week active component SEA
classes are not guaranteed. SEA candidates must have approved orders prior to starting the Blackboard
portion. SEA candidates that start Blackboard exercises without approved orders will not be funded to
attend the in-residence portion on ADT-Schools orders and, per SEA guidelines, must restart the course
from the beginning at a future scheduled convening date. SEA candidates can register via the SEA
website: https://www.NETC.Navy.mil/SEA/SEA-Registration/.
(6) Chief Petty Officer (CPO) Initiation. CPO Initiation will be conducted per reference (o).
(a) Funding. COMNAVRESFOR N7 will fund next-FY CPO selectees to attend the
“Teaching to the Creed” five-day course, subject to ADT-Schools funding availability. All orders must
be submitted to COMNAVRESFOR N7 in conjunction with other CPO Initiation guidance. Formal
facilitators for Teaching to the Creed will be funded using ATPs, subject to availability, and centrally
managed through COMNAVRESFOR. In keeping with Naval Education and Training Command
(NETC) standards, COMNAVRESFOR will fund two instructors per 16 selectees at each training
location. Limited additional IDT periods are allotted to the Force Master Chief account to support CPO
Initiation events. Navy Reserve Centers (NRC) in remote locations where manning is limited will receive
ADT-Special funding on a case-by-case basis. Note the following event-specific guidance.
(b) Heritage Events. Annually, the Navy sends a limited number of CPO selectees to
participate in a heritage event aboard USS Constitution and USS New Jersey (BB-62). These are the only
heritage events authorized for funding using AT or ADT-Special.
(c) Team Building, Networking, and Mentorship Events. While valuable to initiation of CPO
selectees, training events occurring between CPO selection and CPO pinning are not designated as formal
Navy training requirements. As such, except for specified heritage events (paragraph 11a(6)(b), above),
these events will not use AT or ADT-Special. Per reference (h), SELRES Sailors participating in training
events must be in an authorized 10 U.S. Code duty status. To maximize participation, CPOs and selectees
will use paid and non-paid IDT periods to account for such training events.
(d) Capstone Event (Final Night). To encourage maximum participation in the CPO
Initiation capstone event, both paid and non-paid IDT periods are authorized for participants. Paid IDT
use requires UMUIC CO/OIC concurrence (for related transfers) and TRUIC CO/OIC approval.
b. Personnel Selection. UMUIC COs/OICs and RPDs must actively participate in SELRES
assignment selection processes. Stakeholders will collaborate to ensure billet descriptions remain up-to-
date in Reserve Force Manpower Tools (RFMT) for officer billets and MyNavy Assignment (MNA) for
enlisted billets. Quarterly, UMUIC COs/OICs and RPDs will rank junior officer applicants in RFMT and
enlisted applicants in MNA. For senior officers, APPLY guidance promulgates annually via
COMNAVRESFOR Notice 5400. See reference (g) 1300-010 for further guidance.

c. Reserve Unit Assignment Document (RUAD) Mana gement. In response to evolving supported
command requirements (not to exceed quarterly), RPDs must actively assess and update assigned RUADs
in conjunction with the supported command’s manpower business practices and battlerhythm events,
